Job Duties

The Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services (DBHDS) is seeking a distinguished and visionary healthcare executive to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Piedmont Geriatric Hospital (PGH), a Joint Commission accredited and CMS certified, 123 bed geropsychiatric hospital. It is the only Virginia state facility that exclusively treats elderly persons aged 65 and over who are in need of inpatient treatment for mental illness. PGH is located in Burkeville, VA is a small historic Nottoway County town known as a peaceful residential community. It offers a quiet, rural environment surrounded by forests and farmland. It’s located near Twin Lakes State Park and is only about 30 minutes from the town of Farmville, which offers additional dining, shopping, and historical sites like the Robert Russa Moton Museum.

As the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), you will lead a high-performing, multidisciplinary team in delivering excellent, person-centered care to individuals with complex behavioral health needs. This position requires a dynamic and results-driven executive with a proven track record of managing large, complex healthcare operations. You will be responsible for ensuring the hospital’s operational efficiency, meeting key performance metrics, providing outstanding care, and supporting sound business and financial decision-making.

Key Responsibilities Include

Leadership & Strategic Oversight: Oversee all aspects of hospital administration, including strategic planning, operations, human resources, finance, and quality improvement. Drive initiatives to enhance patient outcomes, operational efficiency, and financial performance. Ensure the hospital meets key performance metrics and quality standards while fostering a culture of excellence and safety.
Operational Excellence: Oversee and manage the administrative and business operations of a complex, multi-faceted hospital. Ensure the delivery of high-quality, trauma-informed, recovery-oriented care that meets the unique needs of civil and forensic patients. Collaborate with stakeholders to optimize workflows, reduce barriers to care, and maintain compliance with state and federal regulations.
Workforce Development: Build and cultivate a dynamic, engaged workforce through effective recruitment, training, and development programs. Lead multidisciplinary teams of behavioral health clinicians, professionals, and administrative staff to create a culture of teamwork, accountability, and employee engagement.
Collaboration & Partnership: Provide effective leadership to a network of diverse groups, including public and private community-based treatment programs and providers. Work closely with other leaders within the state hospital system, community providers, law enforcement, judicial entities, and advocacy groups to ensure a comprehensive approach to behavioral health care delivery. Actively participate in statewide planning efforts to advance best practices across the healthcare continuum.
Financial & Performance Management: Oversee the hospital’s $59 million annual operating budget, ensuring fiscal responsibility and financial sustainability. Analyze and synthesize large amounts of data to develop logical conclusions, recommendations, and solutions for enhancing operational performance. Drive cost-effective, data-driven decision-making while maintaining high standards of care.
Innovation & Quality Improvement: Lead initiatives to drive quality improvement, with a focus on patient safety, evidence-based practices, and continuous performance enhancement. Guide the hospital through initiatives to achieve and maintain Centers for Medicaid and Medicare (CMS) deemed status certification.
Policy Interpretation & Implementation: Interpret and apply policy effectively, ensuring alignment with state regulations, accreditation standards, and best practices. Support the implementation of new policies and procedures to improve patient care and operational efficiency.

This is a unique opportunity to lead a distinguished hospital within the Commonwealth’s state hospital system and make a lasting impact on the lives of individuals requiring specialized care. If you are an experienced healthcare leader with a passion for improving the lives of those with complex behavioral health needs, we encourage you to apply.

DBHDS is committed to ensuring that individuals with behavioral health needs receive high-quality, compassionate care across a continuum of services. As part of the state hospital system, PGH is integral to this mission, ensuring that care is safe, effective, and aligned with best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

Leadership Experience: Significant experience in the management and administration of a behavioral health organization, with a progressive career trajectory in healthcare leadership.
Expertise in Behavioral Health: In-depth knowledge of trauma-informed, recovery-oriented care, as well as strategies for managing forensic populations and meeting the specific needs of civil and forensic patients.
Operational Acumen: Proven ability to lead and manage multifaceted healthcare operations, with a strong focus on financial management, workforce development, and achieving operational goals. Experience with budget oversight, fiscal management, and efficient operations is essential.
Strategic and Visionary Thinking: Expertise in strategic planning, change management, and systems thinking, with a demonstrated ability to drive large-scale improvements across an organization.
Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement: Ability to lead and effectively communicate with diverse groups, including facility staff, consumers, families, advocacy organizations, elected officials, and community-based providers. Experience in fostering collaboration across multi-disciplinary teams and external partners.
Healthcare Management Experience: Prior experience in inpatient behavioral health hospital leadership, particularly in forensic and geropsychiatric care.

Additional Considerations

Certification in behavioral health or relevant leadership certifications.

Special Instructions

You will be provided a confirmation of receipt when your application and/or résumé is submitted successfully. Please refer to “Your Application” in your account to check the status of your application for this position.

For consideration, interested applicants must apply by completing the online application and/or submit a resume. However, emailed, faxed, and hand-delivered applications and/or resumes will not be accepted. Applications must be submitted by 11:55 p.m., on the listed closing date. About The Job

Please include a resume and cover letter to be considered. Application review will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. For best consideration, apply by September 8, 2026.

The Opportunity

The University of Minnesota Duluth (UMD) seeks an innovative and collaborative leader to serve as its Executive Director of Admissions during a period of significant institutional opportunity and transformation.

The successful candidate will join a university that views enrollment as a strategic driver of institutional vitality, academic innovation, financial sustainability, and student success. This leader will play a central role in advancing recruitment strategies, strengthening student conversion, cultivating meaningful partnerships, and positioning UMD for continued success in an increasingly competitive higher education landscape.

This is an opportunity to inherit a talented admissions team and lead the continued evolution of admissions through innovation, collaboration, and thoughtful leadership.

Executive Search Information

To learn more about this executive leadership opportunity, the University of Minnesota Duluth, and the search process, please visit the Executive Director of Admissions search website .

Position Summary

The Executive Director of Admissions serves as the university's senior admissions leader, providing strategic leadership for the admissions enterprise. Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Enrollment Management, the Executive Director leads first-year, transfer, and international recruitment while providing executive oversight for admissions strategy, operations, partnerships, and organizational effectiveness.

Working collaboratively with academic and administrative leaders across the university, the Executive Director develops and implements recruitment strategies, strengthens the prospective student experience, advances data-informed decision-making, fosters innovation across the admissions enterprise, and cultivates a high-performing admissions organization that advances institutional enrollment priorities.

In collaboration with graduate education and program leadership, this position serves as a strategic thought partner by identifying opportunities to strengthen graduate recruitment strategies and build organizational capacity for future enrollment growth.

Leadership Opportunities

The Executive Director Will Have The Opportunity To

Lead Strategic Recruitment

Lead the university's admissions recruitment strategy by helping UMD respond to demographic change, evolving student expectations, and increasing competition. Expand market reach, diversify recruitment pathways, and advance institutional enrollment priorities while helping guide the integration of Postsecondary Enrollment Options (PSEO), College in the Schools, and related outreach initiatives into Admissions.

Advance Student Conversion

Champion an integrated recruitment and conversion strategy that helps prospective students confidently choose UMD. Elevate visitor experiences, personalized engagement, faculty, alumni, and student connections, and other touchpoints that influence enrollment decisions while creating a seamless transition from first inquiry through enrollment and the beginning of the student experience.

Strengthen Academic Partnerships

Partner with colleges, faculty, and academic leadership to align recruitment strategies with evolving student interests, workforce needs, market opportunities, academic modalities, and future program development. Support the continued evolution of graduate recruitment through collaborative partnerships with graduate programs and academic leadership.

Modernize the Admissions Enterprise

Lead the continued evolution of the admissions enterprise by enhancing organizational effectiveness, operational processes, policies and procedures, territory management, CRM capabilities, and data-informed decision making while thoughtfully integrating emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Cultivate a university-wide culture where recruitment is viewed as a shared responsibility and continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

Represent UMD Beyond Campus

Serve as a visible ambassador for the university by cultivating relationships with schools, counselors, community organizations, alumni, employers, regional partners, and civic leaders. Advance partnerships that strengthen UMD's visibility, reputation, educational access, workforce development, and long-term enrollment success.

Location and Work environment: Primarily in-person on the University of Minnesota Duluth campus. May be some flexibility for hybrid work.

Work Schedule: Typical business hours, Monday through Friday.

Primary Responsibilities

Admissions Strategy and Planning (20%)
Lead the development and implementation of admissions and recruitment strategies aligned with institutional enrollment priorities
Translate Strategic Enrollment Management priorities into actionable recruitment plans and measurable outcomes.
Advise university leadership on enrollment trends, demographic shifts, market conditions, recruitment performance, and competitor activity to inform institutional decision-making
Facilitate the development, communication, and assessment of undergraduate enrollment targets in partnership with academic leadership and campus stakeholders
Collaborate with the Office of Institutional Research, the budget & analysis office, and external partners to develop enrollment projections, scenario modeling, tuition revenue analysis, and long-range enrollment planning
Lead enrollment analysis related to recruitment performance, student behavior, market trends, and enrollment funnel outcomes to support strategic planning and financial sustainability
Contribute to institutional discussions related to enrollment strategy, academic planning, resource allocation, and long-term university priorities

Recruitment and Student Conversion (20%)
Lead recruitment strategy for first-year, transfer, and international student populations through territory management, market expansion, lead generation, and outreach initiatives
Develop strategies that strengthen application generation, student conversion, yield, and enrollment outcomes
Partner with Enrollment Marketing and Communications to align recruitment strategy, communications, market positioning, and prospective student engagement
Collaborate with Financial Aid and Scholarships to inform financial aid leveraging and optimization strategies in consultation with the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Enrollment Management and the budget & analysis office
Coordinate cross-functional recruitment efforts with strategic enrollment management, academic, student life, and other campus partners to strengthen enrollment outcomes and the prospective student experience
Provide strategic oversight of international recruitment in partnership with International Programs and Services, and collaborate with graduate and professional programs to strengthen recruitment strategies and advance enrollment growth across student populations
Partner with University Marketing and Public Relations to ensure alignment between recruitment strategy, institutional messaging, and brand positioning

Partnerships and Pathways (20%)
Develop and strengthen partnerships with school districts, community colleges, community organizations, and other external partners to support recruitment, educational access, and enrollment goals
Advance transfer pathways, articulation agreements, and other partnership models that strengthen long-term enrollment opportunities
Provide strategic leadership for the integration of Postsecondary Enrollment Options (PSEO), College in the Schools, and related outreach initiatives as organizational responsibilities evolve
Align campus outreach, youth engagement, and pathway initiatives with institutional enrollment priorities to strengthen long-term recruitment pipelines and institutional awareness
Partner with academic leadership to align recruitment strategies with workforce needs, evolving student interests, academic program priorities, and future program development

Enterprise Modernization and Operational Excellence (20%)
Provide strategic leadership for undergraduate admissions operations, including recruitment operations, application processing, analysis, territory management, and visit programs
Lead modernization of admissions systems, operational processes, policies, communication strategies, and organizational workflows to improve effectiveness and scalability
Ensure effective use of CRM systems, enrollment technologies, data infrastructure, and performance metrics to support strategic decision-making and continuous improvement
Utilize data analysis and enrollment insights to evaluate recruitment effectiveness, identify opportunities, and improve organizational performance across the enrollment funnel
Lead process improvement initiatives and evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to strengthen recruitment strategy, operational effectiveness, and the prospective student experience
Manage budgets, staffing models, and resource allocation to support organizational priorities and enrollment outcomes

Organizational Leadership and Talent Development (10%)
Provide strategic leadership and organizational direction across the admissions enterprise
Recruit, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing admissions team while fostering collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement
Establish a distributed leadership model with clear ownership and decision-making across functional areas
Assess organizational structure and recommend improvements that enhance effectiveness, scalability, succession planning, and future organizational capacity

Community and External Engagement (10%)
Represent the university in regional, state, and national organizations, professional associations, and strategic partnerships
Serve as a spokesperson for admissions, enrollment, and recruitment initiatives through media interviews, public communications, and community engagement
Represent the university in public discussions related to admissions strategy, student access, and institutional enrollment growth
Strengthen relationships with school counselors, school and district leaders, employers, alumni, civic leaders, community organizations, and educational partners to advance the university's visibility, recruitment efforts, and strategic partnerships

Other Duties

Experience leading strategic initiatives, operational planning, or organizational projects within a complex organization

We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

What we offer

Impact - The work you do here matters to millions.
Growth - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
Diversity & Inclusion - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
Benefits - We care about your well-being.

Agency Description

The Office of Emergency Management (OEM) collaborates with governmental and non-governmental partners to mitigate, plan, and prepare for emergencies; educate the public about preparedness; coordinate response and recovery efforts for emergencies and complex events; and develop tools and resources to support the City of Philadelphia's overall preparedness.

All OEM personnel must be City residents within six months of hire and are required to serve periodically in an on-call capacity on field response teams. OEM staff also periodically work during non-business hours for extended periods of time, as needed in a field environment, and during activations of Philadelphia’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

Job Description

Position Summary

The Assistant Deputy Director helps to lead OEM's preparedness, response, and recovery for all threats and hazards in the City of Philadelphia. This essential position will assist with the implementation, and evaluation of an integrated program. Providing strategic support to the Deputy Director or First Deputy Director, the Assistant Deputy Director will focus on areas of health and human services, infrastructure, community engagement, homeland security, training and exercises, GIS, continuity of operations, logistics, and private sector coordination among other.

Candidates should possess a strong desire to work in a team-oriented, fast-paced, flexible, and professional public service environment, and a willingness to serve the public in the sixth-largest city in the nation. The ideal candidate is self-motivated, solutions-oriented, easily adapts, has diverse project management experience, anticipates needs, and brings a robust set of soft skills including integrity, diplomacy, communication, and persuasion.

Essential Functions

Under the direction of the Deputy Director, the Assistant Deputy Director will perform a range of activities including, but not limited to, the following key functions:

Working closely with the office’s leadership to support daily and special operations.
Special Projects and Initiatives
Interagency Coordination to include engagement with local, state, federal and non- profit partners.
Work with the Planning Division team to develop and maintain emergency response plans
Support the recruitment and hiring process for staff as needed
Support the development of key performance indicators and objectives along with the maintnance of the multi-year strategic plan
Crisis management and Leadership
Serve on-call as an OEM Response Executive, managing the on-call team and overseeing the entire agency’s response and recovery roles during emergencies, disasters, and large planned events.
Find opportunities within OEM and across its partners to ensure operational readiness for Philadelphia’s risks.
Provide guidance and direction to staff, through modeling and coaching, to ensure effective decision-making and coordination.

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

COMPETENCIES

The ideal candidate:

Exhibits high emotional intelligence and relies on interpersonal, leadership, diplomacy, and negotiation skills to accomplish work.
Communicates clearly and thoroughly in writing and speaking, anticipating the needs of their audience.
Pays keen attention to details to ensure standards are met, as well as find replicable best practices and to conduct root-cause analysis for improvement planning.
Produces projects on-time and within scope based on a stated mission or objective and without significant oversight.
Embraces challenges and provides viable solutions to project impediments.
Exercises discretion to maintain confidentiality and in navigating sensitive topics with different audiences.
Can apply technology to accomplish work, including Microsoft Office Suite, mapping software, web-based platforms for information management and display, and other mediums like audio-visual to convey information.
Applies equity and inclusion lenses in all projects.

KNOWLEDGE

Comprehensive understanding of emergency management principles, practices, and regulatory frameworks, including the National Incident Management System.
Familiarity with local government operations, public safety agencies, and intergovernmental relations.
Knowledge of project management and strategic planning tools and frameworks.

Skills

Time management, self-motivation, and accountability: You know what needs to get accomplished and you are able to manage and prioritize your time to ensure you are meeting expectations. You aim to deliver early and you communicate when plans need to change or a breakdown in expectations occurs.  
Problem-solving, critical thinking, and intuition: You are able to see the whole situation, seek and use existing frameworks for new problems, and conduct your own research to answer questions and propose viable solutions. When the script ends, you can quickly draw on multiple sources to have a plan.
Communication and organization: You are methodical and consistent in how you organize and share information. This standard way of operating helps others to predict and organize their actions.
Diplomacy and emotional intelligence: The nature of emergency management work presents tense situations due to time urgency, resource gaps, and competing priorities. You rely on interpersonal skills to navigate these situations and find a way to ‘get to yes’ as best as possible. You know that your power and authority come through collaboration.
Service: You know that service can take many forms and that most acts of service go unrecognized. Helping a colleague or taking extra time to explain a complex subject to someone is standard practice for you.

Abilities

Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously and pivot quickly.
Ability to operate in chaotic or uncertain environments.
Ability to maintain effective working relationships and develop partnerships.
Ability to coordinate diverse groups toward a common goal.
Sound judgement and ethical, decisive decision-making.
Ability to interpret regulations or policy and program requirements into workflows.
Ability to lead strategic planning efforts to turn ideas into outcomes.

Qualifications

Completion of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. Master’s level education is preferred, but not required.
Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience, or, 4 years of experience in emergency/crisis management, business continuity, public safety, or public administration, combined with graduate-level education.
Minimum of 2 years management/supervisory experience is required.
Minimum of 2 years project management experience is preferred.
Familiarity with the City of Philadelphia is preferred.
Professional certification in emergency management, project management, or business continuity is highly desirable.
Experience engaging a diverse group of stakeholders through program planning and policy development is preferred.
Experience developing, training, and exercising plans is preferred. 
Experience with the National Incident Management System is preferred.
Experience with disaster and relief operations is preferred.
Experience planning and executing large events is preferred.

An equivalent combination of education and experience in a related field will be considered with approval by OEM and the Office of Human Resources.

Additional Information

TO APPLY:
Interested candidates must submit a cover letter and resume.

Salary Range: $110,000- $119,000

Transportation: City employees get unlimited FREE public transportation all year long through SEPTA’s Key Advantage program. Employees can ride on SEPTA buses, subways, trolleys, and regional rail for their daily commute and more.
Parental Benefits: The City offers its employees 8 weeks of paid parental leave.

Our wellness program offers eligibility into the discounted medical plan

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Marketing and Communications advances the visibility of the College of Humanities and Fine Arts (HFA) at UMass Amherst. Spanning a remarkable range of departments, institutes, and centers, HFA offers an exceptionally rich and varied storytelling landscape. Reporting to the Director of Marketing and Communications, this position is a key part of the College's communications efforts, creating and executing content across web, social media, print, photography, and video to enhance HFA’s visibility to both internal and external audiences and advance the strategic goals of the College and University.

Essential Functions

Writes copy for a range of communications purposes, including web pages, social media, newsletters, promotional materials, press releases, and marketing collateral, in alignment with HFA brand standards. Researches and interviews faculty, students, staff, and alumni to develop feature stories, profiles, and news items for the HFA website, and other communications channels.

Assists in the production and distribution of the College’s electronic newsletters and other recurring communications. Contributes writing, proofreading, editing, and design support to a variety of internal and external communications materials for accuracy, consistency, and alignment with College and University style standards.

Assists the Director in coordinating with campus partners, including University Marketing and Communications and the Office of News and Media Relations, to ensure alignment with institutional standards and messaging and to support the promotion of HFA stories.

Supports the day-to-day management of the College’s social media presence across platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Bluesky, while working within the content strategy established by the Director. Stays current with evolving social media platforms, trends, and best practices and provides relevant insights and recommendations to the Director.

Creates and maintains content calendars to maximize content across channels and audiences. Schedules and publishes content in a timely and consistent manner and maintains an organized digital archive of text, photo, and video assets.

Monitors communications metrics and continually improves content based on performance data. Generates periodic reports for review by the Director and College leadership.

Creates graphic design assets for digital and print use, including social media graphics, flyers, banners, postcards, presentations, and newsletters, in accordance with HFA and University branding standards. Assists the Director with photography and videography to support College communications initiatives.

Serves as a resource for communicators and staff across HFA by providing hands-on assistance with writing, design, web content, and social media in alignment with College and University brand standards. Assists departments in executing communications projects consistently and in a manner that reflects the quality and standards established by the Director. Assists the communications team in training departmental staff on College and University communications tools, platforms, and brand guidelines.

Supervises communications student interns and student employees by assigning projects, providing day-to-day direction, monitoring progress, and supporting professional development.

Assists with College events by providing communications, photography, and related support as needed.

Performs related duties as assigned or required to meet College or University goals and objectives.

Understands responsibilities with respect to conflicts of interest and behaves in ways consistent with both the law and University policy.

Contributes to creating a positive and respectful workplace defined by personal and professional competence, integrity, and collaboration.

Understands and contributes to the implementation of departmental and institutional goals for achieving non-discrimination and fostering a respectful, inclusive environment that supports diversity.

Uses access to sensitive and/or non-public University-related information only in the performance of the responsibilities of the position and exercises care to prevent unnecessary disclosure to others.

Excellent writing and editing skills with the ability to produce clear, compelling, and accurate content for a variety of audiences, channels, and formats.

Advanced knowledge of digital content creation and experience with current media technologies, including web, social media, and email marketing. Willingness to learn new technologies as they emerge.

Expertise with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Canva, and Adobe Creative Suite.

Job Title:
Hybrid Community Services Program Director Department:

Summary

Program Directors (PD) manage and support a caseload of community services individuals, providing care and support to adults and minors with developmental disabilities. Due to the nature of the program hours may be flexible and are based upon the needs of the program and needs of the people and employees supported.

Supervisory Responsibilities
Directly supervises Direct Support Professionals and Employment Specialists assigned to the caseload. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Basic Qualifications
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. In addition to the requirements below, the employee must be at least 21 years of age, have a nurturing and caring demeanor, and have a genuine interest in supporting the independence of those we serve.

Education And/or Experience

High school degree or equivalent required
Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university is strongly preferred.
A minimum of 2 years of experience working in the human services field and a minimum of 2 years of supervisory experience is required.
Experience providing direct care service is also strongly preferred.

Trainings, Licenses, and Certifications

Certified Employment Support Professional (CESP) certification required.
40-hour ACRE Certification required.
Bello Machre Orientation, Developmental Disabilities Orientation, First Aid, CPR, MANDT, Certified Medication Technician Training, and Supervisory Training (These trainings may be provided upon hire).
The employee must have and maintain a valid driver’s license. They may not have more than five points on their license at any time and may not have any alcohol and/or drug related citations on their license.

Work Environment

Bello Machre provides a safe, friendly, and supportive work environment. The employee must represent the company’s mission to enrich the lives of those we serve through loving care, guidance, and opportunity so that they can live life to its fullest. Our employees share a dedication to their job and a nurturing spirit that is evident in their everyday work.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk, hear, stand, walk, sit, bend, lift, push, pull, and reach with hands and arms. The employee may be required to perform lifts/transfers and must be able to lift at least 50 pounds.

The employee must maintain skills necessary to safely and efficiently operate various types of equipment to perform their job, which may include the use of wheelchair vehicle safety systems.

Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be in a variety of locations and conditions, including but not limited to the home, various offices, and out in the community. The employee may travel by automobile and may transport those we serve to varying distances and locations.

OSHA
Employees in this position perform tasks that may involve potential exposure to blood and other bodily fluids. All employees are expected to utilize universal precautions and follow all safety guidelines. All employees are offered the opportunity to obtain the Hepatitis B vaccination at no cost to them, and at any time during their employment.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an employee must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

Provide outstanding support and services for people with developmental disabilities, enabling them to participate as fully as they wish in all aspects of community life; Support and advocate for them in relation to their freedom of choice and fundamental rights; Support and promote them by providing choice in all aspects of their lives. Assists individuals in the development of friendships and other relationships; Assists individuals to become an active participant in their community and to build natural support networks; Assists individuals to maximize independence.
Ensure Person-Centered Plans (including behavior plans and medication plans, if applicable) is up-to-date and accurately reflects each individual on the supported caseload. Ensure employees are well trained and are implementing the plan(s), which encourages each person’s ability to maintain the highest practical physical, mental, and psychosocial well-being. Ensure proper distribution and documentation to all involved parties is completed within the designated time.
Maintain the comfort, privacy, and dignity of each person in the delivery of services to them; Interact with each person in a manner that displays warmth and promotes a caring environment. Fully understand all aspects of fundamental rights, including the right to be free from restraints and free of abuse; Responsible for promptly reporting to the appropriate chain-of-command and according to regulations any staff incidents or evidence of abuse or neglect. Ensure proper reporting of incidents are reported, investigated and areas of concern corrected.
Ensure the health and well-being of each person supported. Report medical concerns, conditions, and changes in health status in a timely fashion through the chain-of-command. Ensure proper documentation and reporting of incidents are reported, investigated and areas of concern corrected. Maintain accurate and up to date clinical files. Consistently respond to medical emergencies effectively and efficiently.
Provide management for each employee under their supervision; Conduct individual supervisory meetings at least bi-weekly, in-service meetings, documenting all meetings appropriately; Provide training, guidance, and support to staff on an on-going basis; Empower and train those being supervised to become effective leaders. Provide clear and concise documentation and follow-up on all employee concerns and disciplinary actions. Ensure staff schedules are accurate and required documentation is provided for personnel files.
Maintain accurate documentation, ensure complete injury and incident reports and other organization records are completed, implemented and action taken, as necessary. Ensure appropriate documentation is valid, accurate and in place for receipts for monies spent and that bills are paid timely, for the program and people supported on caseload. Ensure all documentation is timely including documentation related to the Person-Centered Plan (PCP).
Communicate and interact positively and effectively with each person, visitors, family members, peers, and supervisors.
Attend mandatory meetings, to include in-services, supervisory meetings, and the annual “Person-Centered Plan” meeting for each person served; Organize and conduct any team meetings on a regular basis to coordinate successful functions of the program.
Manage caseload schedule to ensure proper coverage at all times; Manage budget hours and overtime while ensuring optimal care and support for the people on the supported caseload. Approve staffing schedules and ensure their accuracy. Utilize Bello Machre’s automated time and attendance system to document and maintain accurate recordkeeping; Communicate with supervisor for any time off needs, change in schedule that may create overtime, and ensure coverage for your shift as appropriate.
Ensure a safe environment where individuals are free from abuse and neglect; Assist individuals in obtaining appropriate medical and therapeutic services; Follow and promote safety practices in the vehicle and community in order to work in a safe and productive manner; Report and correct potentially hazardous situations; Participate in all safety-related trainings.
Conduct and/or oversee monthly and/or quarterly audits of caseload as assigned; report any needed corrections accurately and timely, ensure proper corrections as needed. Paperwork must be reviewed, signed, and submitted as necessary in a timely manner. Proper signature of audited material must be maintained in a timely fashion (petty cash review, mileage logs, training control sheets).

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer - ASC Operations SWOT
jobs.description:
Atlas Healthcare Partners exists to form strategic partnerships with health systems across the nation to develop, manage and operate Ambulatory Surgery Centers (ASCs) in their markets. As a key player in this rapidly growing healthcare segment, we are committed to providing exceptional care and outstanding customer service to every patient, every physician, every time. Our daily focus revolves around our core values of Integrity, Culture, Teamwork, Respect, and Results.

In addition to fostering a workplace that encourages professional growth and advancement, we provide industry-leading health and dental benefits, paired with a matching retirement package. We look forward to you being a vital part of our journey in shaping the future of healthcare.

Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer – ASC Operations SWOT is a high-impact executive leader responsible for rapid deployment to ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) requiring urgent stabilization, optimization, or transformation. This role demands a dynamic operator capable of diagnosing systemic issues, implementing corrective strategies, and driving measurable improvements in clinical quality, financial health, operational efficiency, and cultural alignment. The SWOT CEO serves as a catalyst for change, ensuring each ASC is positioned for long-term success and compliance with regulatory and accreditation standards.

Essential Functions

Lead operational turnaround and performance optimization initiatives across clinical, administrative, and financial functions, with an expectation to achieve full operational readiness within 30 days of deployment, drive improvement in efficiency metrics within 90 days, and record measurable scorecard gains in at least three performance domains within 60 days.
Diagnose root causes of operational inefficiencies and implement corrective action plans that restore stability and foster continuous improvement, completing comprehensive root-cause analyses within 10 business days, executing at least 80 percent of identified corrective actions within 30 days, and resolving 90 percent of critical issues within 60 days.
Oversee day-to-day operations to ensure safe, efficient, and cost-effective surgical services aligned with company mission, vision, values, and patient care standards, targeting an operating room utilization rate of at least 75 percent, an on-time case start rate of 90 percent or higher, staff turnover below 10 percent annually, and patient satisfaction scores of 85 percent or greater.
Implement best practices in operating room utilization, scheduling, supply chain management, and staffing to minimize waste and maximize throughput, maintaining a case cancellation rate at or below 2 percent, benchmarking supply cost per case in the top quartile of national peers, sustaining scheduling accuracy at 95 percent or higher, and aligning staffing ratios with specialty-specific benchmarks.
Monitor and analyze key performance indicators for quality, financial, and operational performance; course-correct proactively to sustain momentum, ensuring 100 percent compliance with weekly KPI dashboard reporting, resolving KPI variances within seven days, and driving month-over-month improvement in at least three core metrics.
Ensure compliance with all state, federal, and accreditation requirements (AAAHC, CMS, state DOH, etc.), achieving zero critical deficiencies in mock surveys, maintaining a 100 percent compliance rate on all official audits and inspections, and securing full annual training completion for every staff member.
Partner with physician leaders, anesthesia providers, and governing boards to sustain high-quality care delivery and physician engagement, working toward a physician satisfaction score of 85 percent or higher, 100 percent anesthesia coverage compliance, and at least 90 percent attendance at quarterly governance meetings.
Lead financial improvement strategies—including cost containment, case mix optimization, and revenue cycle efficiency—to enhance profitability, targeting a 10 percent increase in EBITDA margin within six months, 5 percent year-over-year growth in revenue per case, days in accounts receivable of no more than 40, and a claims denial rate of 5 percent or less.
Manage vendor contracts, negotiations, and facility service agreements to optimize value and service quality, delivering at least 8 percent annual cost savings through renegotiation, achieving a vendor performance score of 90 percent or above, and completing contract renewals within a 30-day cycle.
Build and reinforce a performance-driven culture through coaching, recognition, accountability, and employee engagement, aiming for an employee engagement score of 80 percent or higher, 100 percent completion of annual performance reviews, at least 75 percent staff participation in development programs, and leadership turnover of no more than 5 percent.
Serve as an integration leader during new acquisitions or leadership transitions, ensuring smooth alignment to corporate standards and culture by executing integration plans within 60 days, attaining a cultural alignment score of 85 percent or above within 90 days, retaining 90 percent of key staff post-integration, and stabilizing operations within 45 days of acquisition.
Perform other duties as assigned, completing ad hoc assignments on schedule and securing stakeholder satisfaction ratings of 90 percent or higher for special projects.

Performs all functions according to established policies, procedures, regulatory and accreditation requirements, as well as applicable professional standards. Provides all customers with an excellent service experience by consistently demonstrating our core and leader behaviors each and every day.

NOTE:
The essential functions are intended to describe the general content of and requirements of this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. Specific tasks or responsibilities will be documented as outlined by the incumbent's immediate manager.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Nursing, Business, or related field.
5+ years of progressive leadership experience in ASC operations or surgical services.
Demonstrated success in operational turnaround, performance improvement, and cost containment.
Strong knowledge of ASC regulations, payer dynamics (Medicare/Medicaid, commercial), and compliance requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree (MBA, MHA, MPH).
Experience in multi-specialty ASC or physician joint venture models.
Expertise in value-based care, bundled payments, and digital health solutions.
Clinical background (DON, RN, or similar) strongly preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ENVIRONMENT FACTORS

OE - Typical Office Environment

Requires extensive sitting with periodic standing and walking.
May be required to lift up to 20 pounds.
Requires significant use of computer, phone and general office equipment.
Needs adequate visual acuity, ability to grasp and handle objects.
Needs ability to communicate effectively through reading, writing, and speaking in person or on the telephone.
Requires travel.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Includes supervisory of all assigned ASC leadership and support staff.

DIRECTLY REPORTING

Operations Leadership

Type Of Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has full managerial scope and authority for employment actions, including coaching, candidate selection, training and development, performance appraisals, work assignments, and disciplinary action.

Leadership will strive to uphold the mission, vision, and values of the organization. They will serve as role models for staff and act in a people-centered, service excellence-focused, and results-oriented manner.

SCOPE AND COMPLEXITY

This role is designed for a transformational leader who thrives in high-stakes environments. The SWOT CEO must demonstrate agility, resilience, and a data-driven mindset to lead ASCs through periods of uncertainty and into operational excellence. Success in this role is defined not only by short-term stabilization but by the creation of scalable systems that ensure long-term growth and sustainability. The SWOT CEO interfaces directly with physicians, anesthesia groups, boards, regulatory agencies, and corporate leadership, ensuring compliance, operational efficiency, and cultural alignment. Success requires adaptability to evolving reimbursement models, healthcare policy shifts, and diverse patient populations.

you take pride in the work, show initiative, and bring a strong drive to hit every install and teardown deadline
Leads teams at every level:
you manage and develop Foremen, Leads, and Technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability across the field workforce

you hold a high bar for detail and quality across every asset, display, and site
An effective communicator:
you articulate ideas clearly and concisely across leadership, the events team, Foremen, technicians, vendors, and venue partners
Adaptable and resilient:
you thrive in dynamic environments, learning quickly and adjusting as conditions change
A multitasking pro:
you manage multiple workstreams efficiently and keep your composure under high-pressure, high-stakes conditions

you need little oversight and can be counted on when the pressure is highest

you treat crew safety, structural integrity, and building and fire compliance as non-negotiable at every site

Deliver a fully operational, show-ready park to the Director of Events and Event Managers each night, and coordinate on any technical needs that arise during show hours

The position requires someone who listens carefully to donors’ interests and motivations, connects those interests with opportunities at the College, and makes philanthropic asks.

With a commitment to the College’s mission, the Director collaborates with Laurel Ridge colleagues and community partners and helps build a culture of philanthropy in which gifts at all levels are valued.

Key Responsibilities

Manage a donor and prospect pipeline with discipline.
Identify prospective donors through networking, referrals, community engagement, and research.
Cultivate prospective donors and steward existing donor relationships.
Personally solicit and secure philanthropic commitments, including major and planned gifts.
Develop and implement strategies to retain and deepen donor relationships and re-engage lapsed donors.
Work closely with the Executive Director and Laurel Ridge colleagues to understand institutional priorities, identify philanthropic opportunities, and connect these opportunities with donor interests.
Develop donor proposals, presentations, solicitations, stewardship materials, and other philanthropic communications
Maintain timely donor and prospect records and document next steps.
Assess fundraising progress and opportunities and recommend strategies to the Executive Director.
Work closely with the Marketing and Communications team to promote philanthropy and the role of the educational foundation.
Participate in planning and supporting Foundation events.
Represent Laurel Ridge at events on campus and in the community.
The position requires frequent travel throughout Laurel Ridge’s service region for donor meetings, college activities, and community events.
Participate in occasional evening and weekend activities as necessary
Perform other duties as assigned.

Position Schedule And Other Considerations

This position requires on-site presence, with one day a week telework. The director’s assigned office is at the Middletown Campus. The position requires frequent travel throughout Laurel Ridge’s service region for donor meetings, college activities, and community events. The position requires occasional evening and weekend activities.

Special Instructions for Applicants

The writing sample should demonstrate the candidate’s ability to communicate persuasively. Examples include donor or client proposals, solicitations, sponsorship requests, stewardship communications, or similar professional correspondence. We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

What we offer

Impact - The work you do here matters to millions.
Growth - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
Diversity & Inclusion - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
Benefits - We care about your well-being.

Agency Description

The Office of Emergency Management (OEM) collaborates with governmental and non-governmental partners to mitigate, plan, and prepare for emergencies; educate the public about preparedness; coordinate response and recovery efforts for emergencies and complex events; and develop tools and resources to support the City of Philadelphia's overall preparedness.

All OEM personnel must be City residents within six months of hire and are required to serve periodically in an on-call capacity on field response teams. OEM staff also periodically work during non-business hours for extended periods of time, as needed in a field environment, and during activations of Philadelphia’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

Job Description

Position Summary

The Assistant Deputy Director helps to lead OEM's preparedness, response, and recovery for all threats and hazards in the City of Philadelphia. This essential position will assist with the implementation, and evaluation of an integrated program. Providing strategic support to the Deputy Director or First Deputy Director, the Assistant Deputy Director will focus on areas of health and human services, infrastructure, community engagement, homeland security, training and exercises, GIS, continuity of operations, logistics, and private sector coordination among other.

Candidates should possess a strong desire to work in a team-oriented, fast-paced, flexible, and professional public service environment, and a willingness to serve the public in the sixth-largest city in the nation. The ideal candidate is self-motivated, solutions-oriented, easily adapts, has diverse project management experience, anticipates needs, and brings a robust set of soft skills including integrity, diplomacy, communication, and persuasion.

Essential Functions

Under the direction of the Deputy Director, the Assistant Deputy Director will perform a range of activities including, but not limited to, the following key functions:

Working closely with the office’s leadership to support daily and special operations.
Special Projects and Initiatives
Interagency Coordination to include engagement with local, state, federal and non- profit partners.
Work with the Planning Division team to develop and maintain emergency response plans
Support the recruitment and hiring process for staff as needed
Support the development of key performance indicators and objectives along with the maintnance of the multi-year strategic plan
Crisis management and Leadership
Serve on-call as an OEM Response Executive, managing the on-call team and overseeing the entire agency’s response and recovery roles during emergencies, disasters, and large planned events.
Find opportunities within OEM and across its partners to ensure operational readiness for Philadelphia’s risks.
Provide guidance and direction to staff, through modeling and coaching, to ensure effective decision-making and coordination.

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

COMPETENCIES

The ideal candidate:

Exhibits high emotional intelligence and relies on interpersonal, leadership, diplomacy, and negotiation skills to accomplish work.
Communicates clearly and thoroughly in writing and speaking, anticipating the needs of their audience.
Pays keen attention to details to ensure standards are met, as well as find replicable best practices and to conduct root-cause analysis for improvement planning.
Produces projects on-time and within scope based on a stated mission or objective and without significant oversight.
Embraces challenges and provides viable solutions to project impediments.
Exercises discretion to maintain confidentiality and in navigating sensitive topics with different audiences.
Can apply technology to accomplish work, including Microsoft Office Suite, mapping software, web-based platforms for information management and display, and other mediums like audio-visual to convey information.
Applies equity and inclusion lenses in all projects.

KNOWLEDGE

Comprehensive understanding of emergency management principles, practices, and regulatory frameworks, including the National Incident Management System.
Familiarity with local government operations, public safety agencies, and intergovernmental relations.
Knowledge of project management and strategic planning tools and frameworks.

Skills

Time management, self-motivation, and accountability: You know what needs to get accomplished and you are able to manage and prioritize your time to ensure you are meeting expectations. You aim to deliver early and you communicate when plans need to change or a breakdown in expectations occurs.  
Problem-solving, critical thinking, and intuition: You are able to see the whole situation, seek and use existing frameworks for new problems, and conduct your own research to answer questions and propose viable solutions. When the script ends, you can quickly draw on multiple sources to have a plan.
Communication and organization: You are methodical and consistent in how you organize and share information. This standard way of operating helps others to predict and organize their actions.
Diplomacy and emotional intelligence: The nature of emergency management work presents tense situations due to time urgency, resource gaps, and competing priorities. You rely on interpersonal skills to navigate these situations and find a way to ‘get to yes’ as best as possible. You know that your power and authority come through collaboration.
Service: You know that service can take many forms and that most acts of service go unrecognized. Helping a colleague or taking extra time to explain a complex subject to someone is standard practice for you.

Abilities

Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously and pivot quickly.
Ability to operate in chaotic or uncertain environments.
Ability to maintain effective working relationships and develop partnerships.
Ability to coordinate diverse groups toward a common goal.
Sound judgement and ethical, decisive decision-making.
Ability to interpret regulations or policy and program requirements into workflows.
Ability to lead strategic planning efforts to turn ideas into outcomes.

Qualifications

Completion of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. Master’s level education is preferred, but not required.
Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience, or, 4 years of experience in emergency/crisis management, business continuity, public safety, or public administration, combined with graduate-level education.
Minimum of 2 years management/supervisory experience is required.
Minimum of 2 years project management experience is preferred.
Familiarity with the City of Philadelphia is preferred.
Professional certification in emergency management, project management, or business continuity is highly desirable.
Experience engaging a diverse group of stakeholders through program planning and policy development is preferred.
Experience developing, training, and exercising plans is preferred. 
Experience with the National Incident Management System is preferred.
Experience with disaster and relief operations is preferred.
Experience planning and executing large events is preferred.

An equivalent combination of education and experience in a related field will be considered with approval by OEM and the Office of Human Resources.

Additional Information

TO APPLY:
Interested candidates must submit a cover letter and resume.

Salary Range: $110,000- $119,000

Transportation: City employees get unlimited FREE public transportation all year long through SEPTA’s Key Advantage program. Employees can ride on SEPTA buses, subways, trolleys, and regional rail for their daily commute and more.
Parental Benefits: The City offers its employees 8 weeks of paid parental leave.
We offer Comprehensive health coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.
Our wellness program offers eligibility into the discounted medical plan
Employees receive paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays
Generous retirement savings options are available
Pay off your student loans faster - As a qualifying employer, City of Philadelphia employees are eligible to participate in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Join the ranks of hundreds of employees who have already benefited from this program and achieved student loan forgiveness.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Marketing and Communications advances the visibility of the College of Humanities and Fine Arts (HFA) at UMass Amherst. Spanning a remarkable range of departments, institutes, and centers, HFA offers an exceptionally rich and varied storytelling landscape. Reporting to the Director of Marketing and Communications, this position is a key part of the College's communications efforts, creating and executing content across web, social media, print, photography, and video to enhance HFA’s visibility to both internal and external audiences and advance the strategic goals of the College and University.

Essential Functions

Writes copy for a range of communications purposes, including web pages, social media, newsletters, promotional materials, press releases, and marketing collateral, in alignment with HFA brand standards. Researches and interviews faculty, students, staff, and alumni to develop feature stories, profiles, and news items for the HFA website, and other communications channels.

Assists in the production and distribution of the College’s electronic newsletters and other recurring communications. Contributes writing, proofreading, editing, and design support to a variety of internal and external communications materials for accuracy, consistency, and alignment with College and University style standards.

Assists the Director in coordinating with campus partners, including University Marketing and Communications and the Office of News and Media Relations, to ensure alignment with institutional standards and messaging and to support the promotion of HFA stories.

Supports the day-to-day management of the College’s social media presence across platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Bluesky, while working within the content strategy established by the Director. Stays current with evolving social media platforms, trends, and best practices and provides relevant insights and recommendations to the Director.

Creates and maintains content calendars to maximize content across channels and audiences. Schedules and publishes content in a timely and consistent manner and maintains an organized digital archive of text, photo, and video assets.

Monitors communications metrics and continually improves content based on performance data. Generates periodic reports for review by the Director and College leadership.

Creates graphic design assets for digital and print use, including social media graphics, flyers, banners, postcards, presentations, and newsletters, in accordance with HFA and University branding standards. Assists the Director with photography and videography to support College communications initiatives.

Serves as a resource for communicators and staff across HFA by providing hands-on assistance with writing, design, web content, and social media in alignment with College and University brand standards. Contributes content, creative assets, and logistical support to college-level outreach and engagement initiatives.

Assists departments in executing communications projects consistently and in a manner that reflects the quality and standards established by the Director. Assists the communications team in training departmental staff on College and University communications tools, platforms, and brand guidelines.

Coordinates and manages content requests, including news, web, social media, events, and other communications needs using designated project management tools to establish timelines, milestones, and deliverables and ensure projects are completed accurately and on schedule.

Supervises communications student interns and student employees by assigning projects, providing day-to-day direction, monitoring progress, and supporting professional development.

Assists with College events by providing communications, photography, and related support as needed.

Other Functions

Performs related duties as assigned or required to meet College or University goals and objectives.

Understands responsibilities with respect to conflicts of interest and behaves in ways consistent with both the law and University policy.

Contributes to creating a positive and respectful workplace defined by personal and professional competence, integrity, and collaboration.

Understands and contributes to the implementation of departmental and institutional goals for achieving non-discrimination and fostering a respectful, inclusive environment that supports diversity.

Uses access to sensitive and/or non-public University-related information only in the performance of the responsibilities of the position and exercises care to prevent unnecessary disclosure to others.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and three years of relevant experience in communications, marketing, advertising, public relations, or a related field.

Excellent writing and editing skills with the ability to produce clear, compelling, and accurate content for a variety of audiences, channels, and formats.

Advanced knowledge of digital content creation and experience with current media technologies, including web, social media, and email marketing. Willingness to learn new technologies as they emerge.

Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to interact effectively and develop and maintain collaborative working relationships with a diverse population of staff, faculty, students, and external constituents.

Excellent time management and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple priorities, organize work effectively, and maintain high standards of accuracy and quality.

Ability to exercise sound judgment and maintain confidentiality.

Expertise with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Canva, and Adobe Creative Suite.

Understanding of publishing and distribution platforms and channels, including email marketing, social media, video, and print.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in higher education or a similarly complex, mission-driven organization.

Genuine interest in and enthusiasm for the humanities and fine arts.

Experience with Marketing Cloud or comparable email marketing platforms.

Experience with social media management tools, such as Hootsuite.

Experience with project management tools, such as Asana.

Experience managing editorial or content calendars across multiple channels.

Experience supervising student workers, interns, or entry-level staff.

Familiarity with analytics tools (e.g., Google Analytics, Meta Insights, or Hootsuite Analytics) and the ability to present performance data clearly.

Interest in and experience engaging youth audiences across digital platforms.

Additional Details

Occasional evening or weekend hours may be required.

Occasional day or overnight travel may be required.

This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.

Work is primarily performed in an indoor university environment and involves lifting and transporting materials or equipment and general physical activity, including prolonged standing, walking, or assuming low postures.

Job Description

Job Title:
Hybrid Community Services Program Director Department:
Community Services

Supervisor:
Director of Community Services FLSA Status:

Summary

Program Directors (PD) manage and support a caseload of community services individuals, providing care and support to adults and minors with developmental disabilities. Due to the nature of the program hours may be flexible and are based upon the needs of the program and needs of the people and employees supported.

Supervisory Responsibilities
Directly supervises Direct Support Professionals and Employment Specialists assigned to the caseload. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Basic Qualifications
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. In addition to the requirements below, the employee must be at least 21 years of age, have a nurturing and caring demeanor, and have a genuine interest in supporting the independence of those we serve.

Education And/or Experience

High school degree or equivalent required
Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university is strongly preferred.
A minimum of 2 years of experience working in the human services field and a minimum of 2 years of supervisory experience is required.
Experience providing direct care service is also strongly preferred.

Trainings, Licenses, and Certifications

Certified Employment Support Professional (CESP) certification required.
40-hour ACRE Certification required.
Bello Machre Orientation, Developmental Disabilities Orientation, First Aid, CPR, MANDT, Certified Medication Technician Training, and Supervisory Training (These trainings may be provided upon hire).
The employee must have and maintain a valid driver’s license. They may not have more than five points on their license at any time and may not have any alcohol and/or drug related citations on their license.

Work Environment

Bello Machre provides a safe, friendly, and supportive work environment. The employee must represent the company’s mission to enrich the lives of those we serve through loving care, guidance, and opportunity so that they can live life to its fullest. Our employees share a dedication to their job and a nurturing spirit that is evident in their everyday work.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk, hear, stand, walk, sit, bend, lift, push, pull, and reach with hands and arms. The employee may be required to perform lifts/transfers and must be able to lift at least 50 pounds.

The employee must maintain skills necessary to safely and efficiently operate various types of equipment to perform their job, which may include the use of wheelchair vehicle safety systems.

Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be in a variety of locations and conditions, including but not limited to the home, various offices, and out in the community. The employee may travel by automobile and may transport those we serve to varying distances and locations.

OSHA
Employees in this position perform tasks that may involve potential exposure to blood and other bodily fluids. All employees are expected to utilize universal precautions and follow all safety guidelines. All employees are offered the opportunity to obtain the Hepatitis B vaccination at no cost to them, and at any time during their employment.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an employee must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

Provide outstanding support and services for people with developmental disabilities, enabling them to participate as fully as they wish in all aspects of community life; Support and advocate for them in relation to their freedom of choice and fundamental rights; Support and promote them by providing choice in all aspects of their lives. Assists individuals in the development of friendships and other relationships; Assists individuals to become an active participant in their community and to build natural support networks; Assists individuals to maximize independence.
Ensure Person-Centered Plans (including behavior plans and medication plans, if applicable) is up-to-date and accurately reflects each individual on the supported caseload. Ensure employees are well trained and are implementing the plan(s), which encourages each person’s ability to maintain the highest practical physical, mental, and psychosocial well-being. Ensure proper distribution and documentation to all involved parties is completed within the designated time.
Maintain the comfort, privacy, and dignity of each person in the delivery of services to them; Interact with each person in a manner that displays warmth and promotes a caring environment. Fully understand all aspects of fundamental rights, including the right to be free from restraints and free of abuse; Responsible for promptly reporting to the appropriate chain-of-command and according to regulations any staff incidents or evidence of abuse or neglect. Ensure proper reporting of incidents are reported, investigated and areas of concern corrected.
Ensure the health and well-being of each person supported. Report medical concerns, conditions, and changes in health status in a timely fashion through the chain-of-command. Ensure proper documentation and reporting of incidents are reported, investigated and areas of concern corrected. Maintain accurate and up to date clinical files. Consistently respond to medical emergencies effectively and efficiently.
Provide management for each employee under their supervision; Conduct individual supervisory meetings at least bi-weekly, in-service meetings, documenting all meetings appropriately; Provide training, guidance, and support to staff on an on-going basis; Empower and train those being supervised to become effective leaders. Provide clear and concise documentation and follow-up on all employee concerns and disciplinary actions. Ensure staff schedules are accurate and required documentation is provided for personnel files.
Maintain accurate documentation, ensure complete injury and incident reports and other organization records are completed, implemented and action taken, as necessary. Ensure appropriate documentation is valid, accurate and in place for receipts for monies spent and that bills are paid timely, for the program and people supported on caseload. Ensure all documentation is timely including documentation related to the Person-Centered Plan (PCP).
Communicate and interact positively and effectively with each person, visitors, family members, peers, and supervisors.
Attend mandatory meetings, to include in-services, supervisory meetings, and the annual “Person-Centered Plan” meeting for each person served; Organize and conduct any team meetings on a regular basis to coordinate successful functions of the program.
Manage caseload schedule to ensure proper coverage at all times; Manage budget hours and overtime while ensuring optimal care and support for the people on the supported caseload. Approve staffing schedules and ensure their accuracy. Utilize Bello Machre’s automated time and attendance system to document and maintain accurate recordkeeping; Communicate with supervisor for any time off needs, change in schedule that may create overtime, and ensure coverage for your shift as appropriate.
Ensure a safe environment where individuals are free from abuse and neglect; Assist individuals in obtaining appropriate medical and therapeutic services; Follow and promote safety practices in the vehicle and community in order to work in a safe and productive manner; Report and correct potentially hazardous situations; Participate in all safety-related trainings.
Conduct and/or oversee monthly and/or quarterly audits of caseload as assigned; report any needed corrections accurately and timely, ensure proper corrections as needed. Paperwork must be reviewed, signed, and submitted as necessary in a timely manner. Proper signature of audited material must be maintained in a timely fashion (petty cash review, mileage logs, training control sheets).
Respond to all phone calls and emails within 24 hours; Ensure that all deadlines are met in a reasonable manner; maintain a clean and organized work area and documentation.
Act as a Direct Support Professional/Employment Specialist in the event a need arises (i.e., essential vacancy on the assigned caseload, during an on-call rotation or during an emergency situation which cannot be resolved by other staffing techniques).
Partner and collaborate with local DORS offices to receive ongoing referrals for Employment Services. Complete all documentation necessary in a timely manner to ensure no interruptions with services and funding occur.
Other duties as assigned.
